about: Our own rubric for an Instagram profile. Each part holds criteria; each criterion is rated met (1), partly (0.5), missed (0) or unseen. basis: platform = rests on something Instagram itself says (see sources); judgement = our own view of what makes a stranger follow. Sources are ids in references/sources.md. scripts/score_profile.py refuses to run unless the points add to exactly 100.

criteria.check: Beside the person's name, the name field holds the words a stranger would type to find this kind of account (the topic, the job, the place), not only a name.
criteria.met: a topic or role word someone would search, e.g. 'Ana | Meal prep for one'
criteria.partly: a word that hints at the topic but nobody searches for it
criteria.missed: only a name, a nickname, emoji or a copy of the handle

criteria.check: The name people already know them by is there, spelled the way they would type it.
criteria.met: real name or brand name in plain letters
criteria.partly: present, but in fancy Unicode letters or an unusual spelling search may not match

criteria.check: Short enough to read in one glance on a phone: about 30 characters or fewer, at most one separator, no more than one emoji.
criteria.partly: a little long or busy
criteria.missed: cut off, stuffed with keywords, or mostly symbols

criteria.check: Easy to say out loud and spell from hearing it once, and matches the name people know. Few dots, underscores or numbers.
criteria.met: say it once and someone can type it
criteria.partly: one awkward dot, underscore or number
criteria.missed: hard to spell, or unrelated to the name

criteria.check: The first line tells a stranger who this account is for and what they get from following, in plain words.
criteria.met: 'Easy dinners for people who hate cooking' style: audience and payoff
criteria.partly: says the topic but not what the follower gets
criteria.missed: a quote, a list of identities, or nothing a stranger can use

criteria.check: The bio contains the words people search for this topic (and the place, for a local business), as plain words within the 150-character limit.
criteria.met: the main search words appear as words
criteria.partly: only as hashtags or vague synonyms

criteria.check: One concrete reason to believe them: a result, a number, a credential, a well-known client, years doing it.
criteria.partly: a vague claim ('expert', 'passionate')

criteria.check: Short lines that scan in two seconds; no wall of text, no line that only holds emoji.
criteria.partly: one long block or filler lines

criteria.check: The bio ends on one thing to do next (tap the link for X, DM a word, start with the pinned post), and the reason to do it.
criteria.met: one clear ask with a reason
criteria.partly: an ask with no reason, or two competing asks

criteria.check: What the ask promises is what the link or the DM actually delivers.
criteria.partly: loosely related
criteria.missed: the ask points nowhere, or somewhere else

criteria.check: At least one link in the Links section (Instagram allows up to 5).
criteria.partly: a URL typed into the bio text, which is not clickable there

criteria.check: The first link, the only one shown in full on the profile, goes to the single most useful destination, and it is labelled so people know what they get.
criteria.met: the top link is the main offer, with a clear title
criteria.partly: a generic link page or homepage first, or an unlabelled URL
criteria.missed: first link is stale, broken or off-topic

criteria.check: Recognisable as a small circle: a clear face (person) or a simple logo (brand), high contrast, nothing small to read.
criteria.partly: busy, dark or far away

criteria.check: A creator or business account whose shown category (if shown) fits what the account posts.
criteria.met: professional account, fitting category or category hidden on purpose
criteria.partly: professional account with a mismatched category
criteria.missed: personal account for someone trying to grow an audience

criteria.check: Highlights are used: stories that answer a newcomer's first questions stay on the profile after they expire.
criteria.partly: one, or several that are leftovers

criteria.check: Each title says what is inside in one or two words that show in full under the circle; no emoji-only titles.
criteria.partly: some vague or cut off

criteria.check: The first highlight is the one a newcomer needs first (what this is, start here, results), not the oldest trip.
criteria.partly: useful ones present but buried
criteria.missed: first ones are personal or stale

criteria.check: Posts are pinned to the top of the grid (up to 3).
criteria.partly: one pinned

criteria.check: The pins do three different jobs for a newcomer: who this is and what the account is about, the best proof (most-shared or best result), and the offer or way in.
criteria.partly: pins are good posts but do the same job, or one is stale
criteria.missed: pins are old announcements or off-topic

criteria.check: The top three rows make the topic obvious at a glance: someone could say what the account is about without opening a post.
criteria.partly: two or three topics mixed

criteria.check: Covers read in the tall profile thumbnail: the subject and any text sit in the centre, nothing important is cropped off the top or bottom.
criteria.partly: some cropped or tiny text

criteria.check: Posted in the last 14 days, at a pace they can keep (no long gaps in the last three months). Instagram gives no required frequency.
criteria.partly: recent but patchy, or steady but not in the last 14 days
